land.text: Kalinga, 'an ancient ruling dynasty of Kalinga after the decline of the Maurya Empire'

predecessors.note: The kalinga dossier ends -171 and names this state as successor: the Kalinga infobox gives '170 BCE: Mahameghavahana (founder)'. This page's own regnal list gives the founder as 140 BCE and the dynasty as 'Established: 2nd or 1st century BC'.

land.text: Odisha, the Kalinga core; the infobox lists the Kushan Empire, the Murunda dynasty and the Gupta Empire as successors

successors.note: 'Samudragupta during his Dakshinapatha expedition, defeated Mahendra of Dakshina Kosala who probably belonged to the Megha dynasty according to a speculation.' The page does not explain how the dynasty ended; the 4th century CE is its infobox 'Disestablished'.

capitals.name: Kalinganagara (near Bhubaneswar)
capitals.note: Infobox capitals 'Toshali; Kalinganagara'. Kharavela 'repaired the gates and buildings of his capital Kalinganagara, which was destroyed by a storm' (Kharavela page). The pages do not locate it; the Hathigumpha inscription is at Bhubaneswar, so the point is the Bhubaneswar area.

correction.text: Kalinga and Odisha, 'all of Odisha and some part of northern Andhra Pradesh' (kalinga dossier from the Kalinga page); held to -51

keyframe_review.note: 1,655,395 km2 (72.2-90.9E, 14.1-29.2N: from the west coast to the Ganges) against the infobox 'Area 700,000 km2' (no year given): ratio 2.4, beyond a factor of two, so the shape is wrong. It is Kharavela's claim ('expanded Kaḷinga as far as the Ganges and the Kaveri'; 'Kharavela's suzerainty could spread over the Deccan from sea to sea', Kharavela page, contested) rather than land held; it overlaps the Shunga and Satavahana shapes. The page says the dynasty 'conquered Kalinga and Kosala'. Corrected to the Kalinga core: the Kalinga shape of -188 plus Odisha (about 170,000 km2 by the gazetteer, 300,000 with South Kosala added later). That is 0.24-0.43 of the infobox figure, which presumably is Kharavela's maximum: the corrected shapes are a floor, not the peak. Held -170..-51, not just -170..-165.

New keyframe -50..109: 'In the first century B.C. [the dynasty] conquered Kalinga and Kosala'; the infobox lists Kharavela at 50 BCE and Kudepasiri at 15 BCE. Chhattisgarh stands for South (Dakshina) Kosala. The area is about 300,000 km2 by the gazetteer against the infobox 700,000 (ratio 0.43).

correction.text: Kalinga and Odisha after the loss of South Kosala

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 110..349: 'South Kosala was later conquered by Gautamiputra Satakarni of the Satavahana dynasty' in the early 2nd century CE; Kalinga remains. The page names no ruler or border after Kudepasiri and ends with a speculative 4th-century link to Mahendra of Dakshina Kosala; unverified.

ledger.note: c. 170 BCE: the Mahameghavahana take Kalinga. The page: 'an ancient ruling dynasty of Kalinga after the decline of the Maurya Empire', 'Established: 2nd or 1st century BC', its regnal list opening with Mahameghavahana (founder) 140 BCE; the Kalinga infobox gives 170 BCE. -170 is Cliopatria's year and the kalinga dossier's handover; the page itself says 140 and no single year.

ledger.counterpart: South Kosala (no state named on the page)
ledger.note: c. 50 BCE: Kharavela's dynasty holds Kosala. 'In the first century B.C. conquered Kalinga and Kosala'; 'The third ruler of the dynasty, Khārabēḷa, conquered much of India in a series of campaigns'; the infobox lists Kharavela at 50 BCE. The page names no state in Kosala.

early 2nd century CE: the Satavahanas take South Kosala. 'South Kosala was later conquered by Gautamiputra Satakarni of the Satavahana dynasty' in the early 2nd century CE. 110 is a rounded year; the Gautamiputra page dates his reign between 60-85 and 106-130 CE.

4th century CE: the dynasty is gone. The infobox gives 'Disestablished: 4th century CE'; the page records only that Samudragupta defeated Mahendra of Dakshina Kosala, who 'probably belonged to the Megha dynasty according to a speculation'. 350 is the middle of the century.

wars.name: Kharavela's campaigns
wars.outcome: Kharavela 'led many successful campaigns against the states of Magadha, Anga, the Satavahanas' and 'attacked Rajagriha in Magadha, thus inducing the Indo-Greek king Demetrius I of Bactria to retreat to Mathura'; in year 2 he sent an army west against Satakarni (Kharavela page).
wars.note: The years are Cliopatria's row (-170..-165), which matches the Kharavela page's Daniélou dating (between 180 and 130 BCE). The infobox of this page puts Kharavela at 50 BCE, and the Kharavela page lists other datings down to the first century CE. No land is said to have been held, so no zone.

wars.name: Gautamiputra Satakarni's conquest of South Kosala
wars.outcome: 'South Kosala was later conquered by Gautamiputra Satakarni of the Satavahana dynasty' in the early 2nd century CE.
wars.note: The years span the Gautamiputra page's reign variants for the early 2nd century (c. 103-127, 106-130); no battle is named.

certainty.note: A dynasty known from the Hathigumpha and Mancapuri inscriptions and its regnal list; no frontier is dated, and the extent claims of Kharavela are contested.

sources.title: Mahameghavahana dynasty
sources.note: Infobox (area 700,000 km2, 2nd or 1st century BC to 4th century CE, regnal list), Kalinga and Kosala, Satavahana conquest of South Kosala.

sources.title: Kharavela
sources.note: Hathigumpha campaigns, capital Kalinganagara, Kudepasiri as Kalingadhipati Mahameghavahana, datings of Kharavela.

notes:
Cliopatria row Mahameghavahana Dynasty -170..-165, 1 shape (1,655,395 km2). Two pages opened (budget 1-2).

Departures from Cliopatria: (1) the shape is replaced by the Kalinga core of about 170,000 km2 (300,000 with South Kosala); the infobox 700,000 km2 lies between that and Cliopatria's 1.66 M (ratio of Cliopatria to infobox 2.4, of the corrected shape 0.24-0.43), so the peak extent is unresolved; (2) the state is extended to 350 CE: the page lists the regnal list to Kudepasiri (15 BCE), a loss of South Kosala in the early 2nd century CE and an infobox 'Disestablished' of the 4th century CE, none of which fits a six-year state; the 350 end is the weakest year of the dossier (confidence 1). If a later source gives a firmer end, only the dissolve event and the 110 keyframe's 'to' change.

Not settled: (a) the founding year (140 BCE here, 170 BCE on the Kalinga page, '2nd or 1st century BC'); (b) the Kharavela datings (Daniélou 180-130 BCE; 'third quarter of the first century BCE'; the infobox 50 BCE), so the wars' years are Cliopatria's; (c) whether the Mahameghavahana are the Kalinga state renamed (a group decision: kalinga ends -171); (d) the regnal list's meaning (the infobox gives 140, 120, 80, 50 and 15 BCE without saying whether they are accessions), so rulers are omitted; (e) the Satavahana mirror of the 110 loss of South Kosala is not in the satavahana-dynasty ledger (its page budget was spent); the sibling Satavahana shapes of -27..126 reach 83.5E and may overlap Chhattisgarh, and the -164..-50 Satavahana shapes overlapped Odisha and were corrected there.
Gazetteer: no new names.
